# JEV-works — orientation for an agent picking this up

> Measuring whether a typed-decision model (Jev, via Vercel AI Gateway) can own real decisions,
> and building a validated library of question sets for it. The distinguishing feature of this
> project is that **the instruments get validated before the results are believed** — most of what
> is recorded here was learned by an instrument being wrong.

Read this file first. Then `NETER.md` (what is true) and `LESSONS.md` (what we got wrong). Those two
are the project; everything else is scaffolding around them.
The cross-repo contract (model pin, key policy, gate names, θ, human gate) is `.jev/README.md` — vendored, do not edit.

## Nine rules that are not negotiable

These were compressed from the first 22 lessons (`LESSONS.md` now holds 47, L1–L47). Each one was learned by violating it.

1. **Ask only literal, single-state questions.** A question needing a comparison, a counterfactual,
   or reasoning across items will sit in the mid band forever. Measured: `neededForGoal` reached a
   decisive answer on 7% of 119 items and never exceeded p=0.67. Relational judgements go in code or
   to a text model. (P21, L3)
2. **Recombine on an aggregate, never on a conjunction of confidences.** Requiring every signal to
   be confident escalated 94% of items and reclaimed 2 tokens. (L1)
3. **Report per-question confidence next to any aggregate.** Ten mid-band inputs sum to a number
   with a confident-looking sign. That sign is an artifact of the weights. (L4)
   And use the right statistic per question type: for `choice`, discrimination is **how many
   distinct keys got selected**, not the dispersion of the top probability — which is ~0 by
   construction because the distributions are near-one-hot. (L24)
4. **Declare a colour AND a polarity per answer.** `boolean→Prob`, `choice→Key+Dist`,
   `score→Level`. `Level→Prob` is forbidden — dividing a rubric level by its maximum asserts equal
   spacing and commensurability with probability. Averaging a cost sub-score with benefit
   sub-scores inverts the signal. Use `question-bank/colors.ts`; it fails the build on both.
   (P22, L17, L20)
5. **Entropy and top probability both flag garbage; entropy's edge is below the noise floor — and
   measure the entropy range first.** On inputs with no right answer it answers confidently anyway
   (p 0.82–0.91 on empty strings and emoji; P5). At n=214 (pre-registered, held-out half) entropy
   separated garbage from clean at AUC 0.978 vs 0.952 for 1−top-p: a real edge (+0.026) but below
   P4's noise floor, zero on a 2-option choice, growing only with option count. The earlier n=10
   "~6× margin where top-probability failed" did not replicate (F2). Post-hoc only: at the
   conventional top-p < 0.8 cut, top-p caught 59% of garbage vs 84% for entropy ≥ 0.30 at the same
   clean cost — so a top-p gate must sit near 1 to work. For well-separated choice criteria it returns
   near-one-hot distributions, so corpus max entropy can be ~0.24 and an `entropy > 0.9` gate never
   fires once. Report max entropy on your corpus before relying on a gate, or it is dead code giving
   you no protection. Entropy also *ranks* ambiguity well (ρ = −0.57 against labeller disagreement)
   while *thresholding* it badly. (P5, P6, P26, L23)
6. **Run a cheap baseline in every experiment.** A regex hit 91.7% on the leads task; the field's
   phishing regex hit 91.8% against 62.6% for one broad model question. Without a baseline you
   cannot tell whether the model was needed. (L6 context)
7. **Never tune a threshold because a result disappointed.** Change the instrument or the question.
   Thresholds are fitted on data you set aside and are not reporting. (L6)
8. **No two thresholds within the noise floor of each other.** The floor is question-shaped (P4
   addendum, A/A n=50): booleans and scores p95 ≤ 0.07, a flat 5-way choice reaches 0.15. The
   original 0.11 was one choice question at n=20. Differences smaller than the floor for that
   question's shape are not differences. (P4)
9. **Verify observable behaviour after any change to a config, a name, or a field.** Three silent
   failures in one session: a config key in the wrong case, a package name that never existed, and
   a field rename that produced `NaN` → a confident wrong verdict. Permissive systems turn mistakes
   into plausible output. (L22)

## Where things are

| path | what it is |
|---|---|
| `NETER.md` | property registry — 35 properties (P1–P35), each with evidence and a status (measured here / corroborated / vendor claim / open) |
| `LESSONS.md` | 47 lessons (L1–L47): what happened, why, and the rule. Attached to the files they govern |
| `program/PROGRAM.md` | the five-experiment programme, with hypotheses and falsification criteria written before any run |
| `question-bank/bank.ts` | nine question sets by context. Each names its `notForJev` judgements and the code that replaces them |
| `question-bank/colors.ts` | the composition algebra. `checkComposition` fails the build on an illegal coercion |
| `question-bank/confidence.ts` | confidence/spread/verdict logic, importable. Returns `INSUFFICIENT-DATA` below 8 observations |
| `question-bank/measure-confidence.ts` | CLI: validate any question set against any corpus, no labels needed |
| `lib/telemetry.ts` | `RunLog` — announce before, stream to JSONL during, reconcile after |
| `triage/` | context pruning: keep / drop / escalate over tool outputs. The reference working example |
| `masked/find-targets.py` | finds categorical fields that can serve as labels. 23 usable targets found locally |
| `leads/` | three-stage lead pipeline. Both diagnosed bugs fixed; see `leads/README.md` for status and limits |
| `pass1/` | 100-question research-window scorer and its results |
| `hekat/` | typed layer for HEKAT chains. `hotkeys.ts` declares colours per hotkey; `check-chain.ts` validates `[R→D→I]` chains via fp-ts `Either`. `FINDINGS.md` records why HEKAT itself is prose, not software |
| `dashboard/build.py` | regenerates `dashboard/index.html` from result files. Idempotent |
| `runs/*.jsonl` | one line per item from every instrumented run. `tail -f` these |

## Running anything

Always call Jev via `import { JEV } from './lib/jev.ts'` and `model: JEV`. Never hardcode a model id.
Backend: direct (TypeSafe API, `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, no expiry) when the key is set, else gateway
(Vercel OIDC in `jev-playground/.env.local`, ~12h). Force with `JEV_BACKEND=direct|gateway`.
Record `JEV_ID` in result files. Price with `JEV_PRICE_ID`.

```bash
cd /Users/manu/JEV-works
node <script>.ts   # direct; for gateway add --env-file-if-exists=/Users/manu/jev-playground/.env.local
```

Gateway 401 means the token expired: `cd /Users/manu/jev-playground && vercel env pull`.
Backends are interchangeable (98.3% verdict agreement, 119 items). Direct is ~2x faster.
Node must be ≥ 22.18 for native `.ts` (`/opt/homebrew/bin/node`); v22.17 fails.

Node runs `.ts` directly. `npx tsc --noEmit` must pass before you consider anything done.

Common tasks:

```bash
# validate a question set before trusting it (no labels required)
node --env-file-if-exists=/Users/manu/jev-playground/.env.local \
  question-bank/measure-confidence.ts CONTEXT_TRIAGE question-bank/states-tooloutputs.json

# find labelled targets in any data
python3 masked/find-targets.py ~/some-dir

# refresh the dashboard
python3 dashboard/build.py
```

## Environment traps specific to this machine

- **`node_modules` disappears mid-session.** Happened three times. Lockfiles survive, so recover
  with `npm install` in the affected project. Do **not** symlink one project's `node_modules` to
  another's — it silently removed `zod` and `vitest` from a sibling and broke its tests. (L11, L21)
- **Node runs TypeScript in strip-only mode.** Constructor parameter properties
  (`constructor(readonly x: string)`) throw `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX`. Use an explicit
  field plus assignment. Bit two separate agents.
- **`> file 2>&1` corrupts the file.** Stderr lands inside the JSON you are about to parse. Use
  `2>/dev/null` or a separate log. (L12)
- **fp-ts 2.x cannot be imported bare under pure ESM.** No `exports` map, CJS under `lib/`, so
  `from 'fp-ts/Either'` is a directory import and throws `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT`. Use
  `'fp-ts/lib/Either.js'` — the CJS interop namespace-imports cleanly.
- **`context7` does not work here.** It is configured in an inert `mcp` block in `settings.json`
  (not a real schema key) and names a package that 404s. Fix:
  `claude mcp add context7 -- npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp`.

## State of play

**Established by measurement:** batching is nearly free to ~32 questions then latency roughly
doubles by 100; state scales sub-linearly to ~24k tokens then fails as an opaque HTTP 500 (count
tokens yourself); the argmax is stable across identical calls but probabilities move (p95 ≤ 0.07 on
booleans/scores, up to 0.15 on a flat 5-way choice); it does not abstain; entropy and top-probability
both flag garbage, entropy only marginally better; naive prompt injection was resisted twice.

**The central open problem:** almost no labelled data exists locally. The one corpus that looked
labelled carried only metadata a pipeline assigned to itself. So no accuracy claim is available for
most tasks, and `NETER.md` P20 stays open. The two escapes are **masking** (a categorical field that
already exists is a label — 23 such targets found) and **consensus distillation** (agreement among
model-diverse labellers). Masking is the only thing that can validate consensus, which is why the
programme runs E1 before E2–E5.

**Leads:** the two diagnosed bugs — a corpus name pool of 231 distinct names for 600 leads, and a
dedup fallback that merged on company name alone — are fixed (unique corpus names; dedup never merges
on name alone), per `leads/README.md`. Its open limit: dedup recall on real resubmissions is unmeasured.

## The one thing to internalise

A confident-looking number is the default output of a broken measurement, not a sign of a working
one. Every defect recorded here produced a plausible number first. Before believing a result, ask
what this same pipeline would have printed if the mechanism were broken — and if the answer is
"something that looks like this", go and check.
